title: Euphemisms & Doublespeak
completion_message: ¡Brillante! Has dominado el arte del 'Corporate Doublespeak' y los eufemismos. Esta habilidad retórica es crucial en las relaciones públicas y en la política corporativa para comunicar malas noticias de manera diplomática y profesional.

parts.visual:
En el nivel C2, es esencial entender cómo las corporaciones usan el lenguaje para suavizar realidades duras (Eufemismos o Doublespeak): 

1. Let go / Let someone go (Despedir a alguien): 
- Eufemismo para 'fire' o 'dismiss'. 
Ej: We had to LET HIM GO due to restructuring. 

2. Right-sizing / Downsizing (Recortes de personal / Reducción de tamaño): 
- Eufemismo para despidos masivos. 
Ej: The company announced a RIGHT-SIZING initiative to cut costs. 

3. Negative growth (Crecimiento negativo): 
- Eufemismo para recesión o pérdida financiera. 
Ej: Our division experienced NEGATIVE GROWTH this quarter.
parts.audio: Welcome to Euphemisms and Corporate Doublespeak. In the C2 level, it is essential to understand how corporations use language to soften harsh realities. Number 1: Let go. This is a polite euphemism for firing someone. For example: We had to LET HIM GO due to restructuring. Number 2: Right-sizing or Downsizing. This is a euphemism for mass layoffs. For example: The company announced a RIGHT-SIZING initiative to cut costs. Number 3: Negative growth. A diplomatic way of saying financial loss or recession. For example: Our division experienced NEGATIVE GROWTH this quarter.

parts.visual:
4. Collateral damage (Daño colateral): 
- Daños accidentales o víctimas no intencionadas (muy usado en relaciones públicas corporativas o política). 
Ej: The local suppliers were just COLLATERAL DAMAGE in the trade war. 

5. Restructuring (Reestructuración): 
- A menudo un eufemismo para despidos, cierres de oficinas o bancarrota. 
Ej: The firm is undergoing a massive RESTRUCTURING process. 

6. Let go of / Part ways with (Separar caminos con): 
- Otra forma diplomática de decir que alguien fue despedido o renunció bajo presión. 
Ej: The board decided to PART WAYS WITH the CEO.
parts.audio: Number 4: Collateral damage. This refers to unintended victims or accidental damage, often used in public relations or politics. For example: The local suppliers were just COLLATERAL DAMAGE in the trade war. Number 5: Restructuring. Often a euphemism for layoffs, office closures, or even bankruptcy. For example: The firm is undergoing a massive RESTRUCTURING process. Number 6: Part ways with. A diplomatic way of saying someone was fired or pressured to resign. For example: The board decided to PART WAYS WITH the CEO.

questions.question: The company didn't say they were firing 500 people; instead, they announced a massive ____ initiative.
questions.explanation: Right-sizing = eufemismo para recortes de personal.

questions.question: Instead of saying 'You're fired', the manager said politely: 'Unfortunately, we have to let you ____'.
questions.explanation: Let someone go = eufemismo para despedir.

questions.question: The press release didn't mention 'losses'; it diplomatically stated that the company experienced ____ growth.
The board issued a statement saying they have mutually decided to ____ ways with the CEO. (Separar caminos / Despedir).
questions.explanation: Part ways with = eufemismo diplomático para un despido de alto nivel.

questions.question: The innocent small businesses that went bankrupt due to the new regulations were referred to as mere ____ damage by the politicians.
questions.explanation: Collateral damage = daño colateral (víctimas no intencionadas).

questions.question: We are not 'closing' branches; we are merely ____ our physical footprint. (Optimizando).
questions.explanation: Optimizing = eufemismo para cerrar, reducir o eliminar para ahorrar costos.

questions.question: The HR department doesn't call it a 'demotion' (descenso de categoría); they call it a '____ reassignment'.
questions.explanation: Strategic reassignment = eufemismo para degradación o traslado forzoso.

questions.question: Instead of 'used car', the dealership sells '____-owned' vehicles.
The military doesn't say 'assassination'; they use the term '____ killing'.
questions.explanation: Targeted killing = eufemismo político/militar para asesinato.

questions.question: In corporate PR, a massive technical failure or disaster is often referred to simply as an '____'.
questions.explanation: Incident = eufemismo para suavizar un desastre o falla grave.

questions.question: Instead of saying 'The project failed miserably', the report stated: 'The project experienced a ____'.
questions.explanation: Shortfall (o setback) = eufemismo para un fracaso o déficit.

questions.question: The company is not going bankrupt; it is undergoing a comprehensive financial ____.
questions.explanation: Restructuring = eufemismo común para bancarrota (ej: Chapter 11) o despidos masivos.

questions.question: They didn't say he was 'lying'; the lawyer argued that his client was merely being 'economical with the ____'.
questions.explanation: Economical with the truth = eufemismo británico famoso para mentir o retener información.

questions.question: The government announced a 'kinetic military ____', which is doublespeak for an act of war or bombing.
questions.explanation: Kinetic military action = eufemismo militar para la guerra.

questions.question: Instead of admitting 'We lost the data', the tech company reported a 'data ____ anomaly'.
questions.explanation: Data integrity anomaly = doublespeak para pérdida o corrupción de datos.

questions.question: The supervisor didn't tell her she was 'incompetent'; he said she had '____ areas for improvement'.
questions.explanation: Areas for improvement = eufemismo para incompetencia o debilidades.

questions.question: Instead of calling it a 'bribe' (soborno), the corrupt official called it a 'facilitation ____'.
The airline didn't say the flight was 'canceled'; they said there was an 'equipment ____'.
questions.explanation: Equipment change (o issue) = eufemismo para esconder que el avión se rompió o el vuelo se canceló.

questions.question: A 'correction' in the stock market is actually a polite word for a sudden drop or ____ in stock prices.
questions.explanation: Market correction = eufemismo para caída del mercado (generalmente >10%).

questions.question: When a company moves jobs to a cheaper country, they don't say 'firing locals'; they call it '____'.
questions.explanation: Offshoring (u Outsourcing) = eufemismos corporativos que implican pérdida de empleos locales.

questions.question: To let someone ____. (Despedir)
To ____ ways with the CEO. (Despedir / Separar caminos)
Right-____. (Eufemismo para despidos masivos)
Negative ____. (Eufemismo para pérdida/recesión)
____ damage. (Daño colateral)
____ reassignment. (Eufemismo para degradación con S)
____-owned. (Eufemismo para 'usado' con P)
An ____. (Eufemismo para un desastre técnico con I)
Economical with the ____. (Eufemismo para mentir con T)
Financial ____. (Eufemismo para bancarrota con R)
